## Q1 | A Price for Brooms

SwiftTech’s methods spread, and now many identical makers sell the same standard broom, so each one takes the market price as given. Each maker has a fixed cost of 360 coins a week, which it must pay this period even if it makes nothing, and a marginal cost:

$$
MC = 5 + \frac{q}{5}
$$

where $q$ is the number of brooms it makes in a week. The table shows its average total cost at some quantities. The graph shows one maker’s marginal cost and average total cost.

::: {.table style=grid density=compact columns="auto 1fr 1fr 1fr 1fr" fills=r0:gray-dark valign=middle}

| **Brooms** | **20** | **40** | **60** | **90** |
| :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **ATC** | 25 | 18 | 17 | 18 |

:::

:::: {.columns gutter=0.5em}

::: {.column width=60%}

If the market price is 23 coins:

a\) Find and graph marginal revenue. 

::: solution

Marginal revenue is the price, 23 coins: a flat line at 23.

:::

b\) Find and graph the firm’s profit maximizing quantity.

::: solution

$P = MC$: $23 = 5 + q/5$, so $q = 90$ brooms.

:::

c\) Find and graph the firm’s maximized profit.

::: solution

At 90 brooms $ATC$ is 18, so profit is $(23 - 18) \times 90 = 450$ coins: the rectangle between the price line and $ATC$, out to 90.

:::

:::

::: {.column width=40%}

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

:::

::::

:::: {.columns gutter=0.5em}

::: {.column width=60%}

If the price falls to 13 coins:

d\) Find and graph the firm’s profit maximizing quantity if they stay open.

::: solution

$13 = 5 + q/5$, so $q = 40$ brooms.

:::

e) Find and graph the firm’s maximized profit if they stay open.

::: solution

At 40 brooms $ATC$ is 18, so profit is $(13 - 18) \times 40 = -200$ coins: a loss of 200, the rectangle between $ATC$ and the price line, out to 40.

:::

f\) What is the firm’s profit / loss if they shutdown?

::: solution

It still pays the fixed cost and sells nothing: a loss of 360 coins.

:::

g\) Should the firm stay open or shutdown?

::: solution

Stay open. It loses 200 instead of 360, because the price of 13 more than covers the variable cost of each broom.

:::

:::

::: {.column width=40%}

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

:::

::::

:::: {.columns gutter=0.5em}

::: {.column width=60%}

In the long run:

h\) Do firms enter or exit at a price of 23 coins? \

::: solution

Firms enter. At 23 each firm earns a profit, which draws new firms in and pushes the price down.

:::
i\) Do firms enter or exit at a price of 13 coins?

::: solution

Firms exit. At 13 each firm takes a loss, so firms leave and the price rises.

:::

j\) Find and graph the long-run price.

::: solution

Entry and exit stop when profit is zero, where the price equals the lowest $ATC$: 17 coins.

:::

k\) Find and graph the firm’s quantity and profit at that price.

::: solution

$17 = 5 + q/5$, so $q = 60$ brooms. Profit is $(17 - 17) \times 60 = 0$: the price line just touches $ATC$, so there is no rectangle.

:::

:::

::: {.column width=40%}

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

:::
